title: All About Earthworms
checkpoint: Phase 5 complete (School readiness) — non-fiction, Phonics Screening Check review week, real facts about earthworms.
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 complete (School readiness) — non-fiction, Phonics Screening Check review week, real facts about earthworms.

pages.text: Moss digs in the soil in the garden bed.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog digging gently with his paws in a patch of dark soil in a garden bed.

pages.text: Moss spots a long, thin worm.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog looking closely at a long, pink-brown worm in the soil.

pages.text: A worm has no legs at all.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the smooth, legless body of the worm curving through the soil.

pages.text: A worm can not see at all.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the worm's smooth, rounded head with no visible eyes.

pages.text: A worm digs new paths under the ground.
pages.illustration: A cutaway view of the soil showing winding tunnel paths made by the worm underground.

pages.text: The paths let air into the soil.
pages.illustration: Small air gaps visible along the worm's tunnel paths in the soil.

pages.text: A worm eats old, soft bits of plants.
pages.illustration: The worm nibbling at old, soft, rotting plant matter in the soil.

pages.text: More worms come up when it rains.
pages.illustration: Several worms coming up near the surface of the garden bed during a light rain shower.

pages.text: Worms help the soil stay good for plants.
pages.illustration: Healthy green plants growing well in the garden bed, worm tunnels visible in the soil beneath.

pages.text: Moss is glad worms help the garden grow.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog standing in the garden bed, looking pleased at the healthy plants growing around him.
